We need propose a retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999. Need to construct JSON route.

We have target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We applied template 827966 which gave product? Actually apply_template returns precursors? It returned a tuple with a SMILES string: 'Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1' That's similar but missing methyl on first phenyl? original target has a tolyl (methyl) on first phenyl. The precursor from template seems to be same but with phenyl not tolyl? Actually original: Cc1ccc... The precursor: Cc1ccccc1... Wait both have Cc1... The returned SMILES: Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1. That is same as target? Let's compare: target: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. The returned: Cc1ccccc1NS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc2ccccc2N)cc1. The difference: In target, the sulfonamide attaches to phenyl ring (para?) but the returned seems same connectivity? Might be same molecule (maybe template just reorders). So template didn't break anything.

We need break bonds to get simpler precursors. Likely disconnection: break sulfonamide N-S bond to get sulfonyl chloride + aniline? Or break amide bond to get aniline and acid? Also break the alkene? The target has a stilbene-like chain: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-phenyl-NH2? Actually /C=C/C(=O)N- phenyl-N. So we could disconnect amide to give aniline (anilide) and acid (cinnamic acid derivative). Also disconnect sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline.

Goal: 3 steps max. Leaves must be commercially available.

Potential route:

Step1: Disconnection of amide: target -> precursor A: 4-(methyl)aniline sulfonyl phenyl (the sulfonamide part) attached to cinnamic acid? Wait amide is between carbonyl and aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually structure: .../C=C/C(=O)N c3ccccc3N. So amide carbonyl attached to aniline that also has an NH2 ortho? Actually N attached to phenyl with NH2 substituent (aniline). So amide precursor: cinnamic acid (or trans-cinnamic acid) + 4-aminophenyl sulfonyl tolyl? Let's think.

Simplify: target = p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to para-phenyl with trans-alkenyl amide to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So we could retrosynthesize:

1) Break amide: give precursor1 = trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated form) and aniline (para-aminophenyl) attached to sulfonyl? Actually amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N) which is an aniline (para-? not substituted). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl ring that also has an NH2 substituent? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with two nitrogens? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" means an aniline where the nitrogen attached to carbonyl is attached to phenyl at position 1, and there is another NH at other position? The SMILES: N c3 c c c c c3 N. That's an aniline with an NH at both ends? It is a phenyl diamine (p-phenylenediamine) but only one N attached to carbonyl, the other is free NH2. So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl that also has an NH2 para? Actually positions not defined.

Thus amide disconnection yields: (a) trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated derivative) and (b) p-phenylenediamine (or 4-aminophenylamine). But the sulfonamide part is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl). So overall we need also break sulfonamide: give sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride) and p-phenylenediamine? Wait sulfonamide nitrogen is same as the aniline that is part of amide? Actually sulfonamide N is attached to the tolyl phenyl and to the sulfonyl group, and also attached to the second phenyl? Let's parse: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl ring (as substituent) and to sulfonyl group which attaches to second phenyl (c2...). That nitrogen is not the same as amide nitrogen. So there are two nitrogens: sulfonamide N (connected to tolyl and sulfonyl) and amide N (connected to carbonyl and phenyl diamine). So we have two disconnections.

Thus route:

Step1: Break sulfonamide: target -> sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride?) Actually sulfonyl chloride would be p-tolyl-SO2-Cl? Wait sulfonyl chloride is R-SO2-Cl. Here sulfonyl group attached to phenyl (c2ccc...). So we could have sulfonyl chloride derived from that phenyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride). The other fragment would be the aniline (p-toluidine) bearing the rest of molecule (including amide chain). So fragment A: p-toluidine with attached amide chain (i.e., p-tolyl-NH-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). That's still complex but maybe we can further disconnect amide.

Thus step2: Break amide in fragment A to give trans-cinnamic acid (or its activated form) and p-toluidine (or p-toluidine with something?). Actually after sulfonamide break, the fragment A still contains the amide chain attached to p-tolyl via NH (aniline). So we can break amide to give trans-cinnamic acid and p-toluidine (which already is the same). So final leaves: p-toluidine (commercial), trans-cinnamic acid (commercial), aryl sulfonyl chloride (commercial). That's 2 steps (two disconnections). Leaves are commercially available and cheap.

We need to verify availability and price. Use is_buyable for each.

Check p-toluidine SMILES: "Cc1ccc(N)cc1". trans-cinnamic acid SMILES: "C=CC(=O)O". Aryl sulfonyl chloride: phenyl sulfonyl chloride? For the phenyl attached to sulfonyl: it's phenyl with para? Actually the sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) which is unsubstituted phenyl. So aryl sulfonyl chloride: "ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1". That's chlorosulfonyl benzene? Actually sulfonyl chloride is "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1". SMILES: "ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1". Yes.

Check buyability.
